title: Light
ks3: Waves: light, reflection, refraction and colour
intro: How light travels, shadows, mirrors, bending light and colour. Practise reflection, refraction, the spectrum and coloured filters.
description: Free KS3 Physics light questions with answers: how light travels, shadows, reflection and the law of reflection, refraction, dispersion, colour and filters. Marked instantly, for Year 7, 8 and 9 (ages 9 to 14).

questions.q: Light travels in…
questions.hint: Think of a torch beam or sunlight through a window.
questions.explain: Light travels in straight lines. That is why it makes sharp shadows and can't go round corners.

questions.q: Which of these is a light source?
questions.hint: A light source gives out its own light.
questions.explain: The Sun makes its own light. The Moon, mirrors and white pages only reflect light from somewhere else.

questions.q: Which material is transparent?
questions.hint: You can see clearly through a transparent material.
questions.explain: Clear glass lets almost all light through, so it is transparent. Wood, metal and cardboard are opaque.

questions.q: How do we see a book?
options: Light bounces off the book into our eyes
Light comes out of our eyes onto the book
The book gives out its own light
The book makes a sound we can see
questions.hint: The book is not a light source.
questions.explain: Light from a source (like a lamp) reflects off the book, and some of it goes into our eyes.

questions.q: Why does a shadow form?
options: Light can't pass through an opaque object
questions.hint: Light travels in straight lines.
questions.explain: An opaque object blocks the light. Light travels in straight lines, so it can't bend round, and a dark area (a shadow) forms behind the object.

questions.q: Light travels at about 300,000 km/s. Sunlight takes about 500 s to reach the Earth. About how far away is the Sun, in millions of km?
questions.hint: Distance = speed × time. Then change to millions.
questions.explain: 300,000 km/s × 500 s = 150,000,000 km, which is 150 million km.

questions.q: Which of these is translucent (lets some light through, but you can't see clearly through it)?
questions.hint: Think of a bathroom window you can't see through clearly.
questions.explain: Frosted glass lets some light through but scatters it, so you can't see clearly through it. Clear glass is transparent; brick and metal are opaque.

questions.q: A pinhole camera is a box with a tiny hole at the front and a screen at the back. What is the image of a tree like on the screen?
questions.hint: Light travels in straight lines. Follow a ray from the top of the tree through the hole.
questions.explain: Light from the top of the tree goes in a straight line through the hole and lands at the bottom of the screen, and light from the bottom lands at the top. So the image is upside down (inverted).

questions.q: Sunlight reaches the Earth through space, where there is no air. What does this show?
options: Light can travel through a vacuum
questions.hint: Space is a vacuum: it has almost no particles.
questions.explain: Light can travel through a vacuum, so it crosses empty space from the Sun to the Earth. Sound can't do this.

questions.q: What does the law of reflection say?
options: Angle of incidence = angle of reflection
questions.hint: Both angles are measured from the normal.
questions.explain: The angle of incidence (the ray going in) equals the angle of reflection (the ray coming out). Both are measured from the normal, a line at 90° to the mirror.

questions.q: A ray of light hits a flat mirror. What is the angle of reflection, r?
questions.hint: Use the law of reflection.
questions.explain: The angle of incidence is 40°, so the angle of reflection is also 40°.

questions.q: You look at yourself in a flat mirror. What is your image like?
options: The same size and the right way up, but left and right are swapped
questions.hint: Raise your right hand in front of a mirror. Which hand does the image raise?
questions.explain: A flat mirror makes an image the same size as you, the right way up, and as far behind the mirror as you are in front. Left and right look swapped (it is laterally inverted).

questions.q: Which surface gives the clearest reflection?
questions.hint: You can see your face in it.
questions.explain: A smooth, shiny surface reflects all the light rays in the same way, so it makes a clear image. Rough surfaces scatter light in all directions, so there is no clear image.

questions.q: A ray of light hits a flat mirror with an angle of incidence of 30°. What is the angle between the reflected ray and the mirror's surface?
questions.hint: First find r using the law of reflection. The normal is at 90° to the mirror.
questions.explain: The angle of reflection r = 30° (measured from the normal). The normal is at 90° to the mirror, so the angle between the reflected ray and the mirror is 90° − 30° = 60°.

questions.q: A ray of light goes from air into a glass block at an angle. What happens?
questions.hint: Light slows down in glass.
questions.explain: Light slows down when it goes into glass, so it changes direction. This is called refraction.

questions.q: A straw in a glass of water looks bent. Why?
options: Light refracts as it passes from the water into the air
questions.hint: The straw is really straight. Something happens to the light.
questions.explain: Light from the part of the straw under water bends (refracts) as it leaves the water, so that part looks as if it is in a different place.

questions.q: A magnifying glass has a convex lens (thicker in the middle). What does it do to rays of light that hit it side by side (parallel)?
options: Brings them together at a point (the focus)
questions.hint: A magnifying glass can focus sunlight into a tiny bright spot.
questions.explain: A convex lens refracts the rays so they come together (converge) at a point called the focus. This is also how the lens in your eye focuses light on the retina.

questions.q: A ray of light goes from air into a glass block at an angle. Which way does it bend?
questions.hint: Light slows down in glass. The normal is the line at 90° to the surface.
questions.explain: When light slows down going into glass, it bends towards the normal. When it speeds up coming back out into the air, it bends away from the normal.

questions.q: A ray of light hits a glass block straight on, along the normal (at 90° to the surface). What happens?
options: It carries on in a straight line without changing direction
It bends away from the normal
questions.hint: Refraction makes light change direction only when it hits the surface at an angle.
questions.explain: Along the normal the ray still slows down in the glass, but it does not change direction. It goes straight through.

questions.q: White light can be split into a spectrum of colours by a prism. What is this called?
questions.hint: The colours are spread out, or dispersed.
questions.explain: Splitting white light into its colours is called dispersion. Each colour refracts by a different amount.

questions.q: Which colour is bent (refracted) the most by a prism?
questions.hint: Look at the bottom of a rainbow made by a prism.
questions.explain: Violet light is refracted the most and red light the least, so the colours spread out in the order red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet.

questions.q: Why does a red apple look red in white light?
options: It reflects red light and absorbs the other colours
It makes its own red light
questions.hint: White light contains all the colours.
questions.explain: The apple's skin reflects red light into our eyes and absorbs the other colours.

questions.q: What colour does a red apple look in pure blue light?
questions.hint: The apple only reflects red light. Is there any red light to reflect?
questions.explain: The apple absorbs the blue light, and there is no red light to reflect, so it looks black.

questions.q: A red filter is put in front of a white lamp. What colour light comes through?
questions.hint: A filter lets its own colour through.
questions.explain: A red filter absorbs all the other colours and only lets red light through.

questions.q: Which list shows the colours of the spectrum in the right order?
options: Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet
Red, yellow, orange, blue, green, violet, indigo
Violet, red, green, orange, blue, yellow, indigo
Green, blue, red, yellow, orange, violet, indigo
questions.hint: Remember "Richard Of York Gave Battle In Vain".
questions.explain: The spectrum goes red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet, the same order as a rainbow.

questions.q: What colour does a white T-shirt look in red light?
questions.hint: A white object reflects every colour that shines on it.
questions.explain: White reflects all colours. Only red light is shining on it, so it reflects red light and looks red.

questions.q: White light shines through a red filter and then through a green filter. What comes out of the green filter?
options: No light, so it looks dark
questions.hint: What does the red filter let through? Then what does the green filter do to that?
questions.explain: The red filter lets only red light through. The green filter only lets green light through, so it absorbs the red light. No light gets through.
